description:
Uploads or replaces one file in the app's draft. Limits: 30 files on free, 150 on Pro, 25 MB per file. Text files (HTML, CSS, JS, TS, JSON, SVG) go as raw UTF-8 text with encoding="utf8" (the default), verbatim. Binary files (images, fonts, audio, video) go as a public URL in `contentUrl`, which Neblla downloads server-side, or as a base64 string in `content` with encoding="base64". Uploading the same path again overwrites the previous version. The file waits in the app's draft (nobody sees it) until neblla_promote({ action: "publish" }) sends the whole draft at once to the app's environment (pro, the users', unless the developer chose pre). An app linked to its own repo (neblla_git) takes each upload as a commit on pre's branch of that repo, then syncs it back (publish then sends it on). 

Canonical paths for a Neblla app are index.html, main.css, client.js (front-end) plus server/lobby.js, server/gathering.js, server/room.js (server-side). The server/ files are special: the SDK loads them itself and runs them in an isolated scope with no DOM access: index.html does not reference them, and they hold no DOM code or window.onNeblla (they are top-level code where `neblla` is in scope as a global). client.js, by contrast, uses window.onNeblla = (neblla) => {…}. Communication between client.js and the server files is messages and state only (message.send / message.to('server' | 'presenter' | id, data) / message.on(m => …) / state.set / state.on), not direct function calls. All three server/ files run on the room's SERVER PEER — a device the SDK elects by latency and CPU, which EXCLUDES only boards, so in peer mode it may well be the presenter. The presenter is a different role: the first device into the room; if it leaves, the SDK promotes another device (chosen like the server peer, not by arrival order) and fires neblla.room.on('presenter'). server/lobby.js for the lobby (matchmaking); server/gathering.js while a non-lobby room is in 'gathering' state (decide when to call neblla.room.start() to start the game); server/room.js after room.start (authoritative game logic — hear players with neblla.message.on(m => { if (m.to !== 'server') return; … }), broadcast with neblla.message.send / neblla.state.set).

content.description: File content. For text files: the raw source as-is (NOT base64). For binary files: a base64 string. Required UNLESS `contentUrl` is set.

contentUrl.description: Public URL of the file to upload. Neblla downloads it server-side (no need to base64-encode in this conversation). Use this for any binary asset (images, fonts, audio, video) when you have a URL. Mutually exclusive with `content`.

encoding.description: Content encoding for `content`. Ignored when `contentUrl` is used. Use "utf8" for all text files (HTML/CSS/JS/TS/JSON/SVG); "base64" only for binary assets.

message.description: A short note about this change. It names this version in the app history (neblla_versions), so the history reads like a changelog instead of "upload: 3 file(s)". A burst of uploads is one version: pass the same note on each.

path.description: File path within the app. Canonical: "index.html", "main.css", "client.js", "server/room.js". Subfolders allowed for assets.
